newsitem.title: USA: NY has yet to agree to bills for Dec session - paper.
newsitem.headline: NY has yet to agree to bills for Dec session - paper.

text.p: Negotiations between New York State lawmakers and the Pataki Administration over a special session expected to start next week have bogged down with no bills agreed to, the Albany Times Union said on Thursday.

The paper, citing lobbyists and government sources, said Gov. George Pataki and Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver disagreed over whether to increase or extend pay for additional duties, like serving as committee chairman.

But it quoted a spokeswoman for the governor as saying she was "totally unware" of any verbal battle between Pataki and Silver over stipends. She also said Pataki was "very optimistic" after meeting with Silver and Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno (R-Troy), on Tuesday.
But Bruno told the paper that while reforming how New York City's schools are govered could be resolved quickly, the sides are still apart on all issues.

The special session no longer is expected to take up welfare reform, but it is anticipated that it will extend a personal income tax for New York City. Bruno told the paper a push to increase legislative salaries had not yet been discussed.
